messages:
Jules Park: Hi team, first morning here. My M2 MBP shows 'Profiles: Pending Configuration' and System Settings has a greyed-out checkbox for FileVault. Also trying to apply the latest macOS update but it says 'A required profile is missing'. Can someone grant admin or tell me what profile is needed?

Sam (IT): Welcome Jules! :wave: Can you paste output of `profiles status -type enrollment` and `fdesetup status`? Also what's the serial (About This Mac)?

Jules Park: Serial C02YQ1ABC123. `profiles status -type enrollment` -> "Device is enrolled: Pending profile installation (MDM: Jamf Pro)". `fdesetup status` -> "FileVault is Off." Update error popup: "A required configuration profile is missing to enable this update."

Rina - Mac Admin: Looks like the MDM profile that contains the kernel-extension approval and system policy isn't applied yet. Sometimes the staging image didn't run the post-enroll hook. Jules, can you run `sudo jamf policy -trigger post_enroll` and paste the short output?

Jules Park: Running it now: `Executing policy post_enroll... Updating inventory... Installing configuration profiles... ERROR: Could not install profile 'com.redwood.security.kext' - 403`

Rina - Mac Admin: 403 on profile install means Jamf server rejected it for this serial (staging hold). I'll check Jamf. mdm-bot, check device record C02YQ1ABC123.

mdm-bot: Jamf lookup: device(C02YQ1ABC123) -> enrollment: pending; staging-hold: true; last check-in: 2026-09-05T07:42:01Z.

Rina - Mac Admin: Aha — device flagged staging-hold which blocks some security profiles until we approve. Jules, confirm you're in-office or on VPN? We only release kext/profile to devices in trusted networks.

Jules Park: I'm remote (home) on a corporate VPN via FortiClient, but maybe autopush didn't mark me as trusted.

Sam (IT): We can do two things: 1) temporarily lift the staging-hold for this serial and push the missing profiles, or 2) create a temporary local admin so you can install Rosetta and the update locally, then we reconcile. Which do you prefer?

Jules Park: Temporary lift would be easiest so everything is managed. I don't want to be admin if we can avoid it.

Rina - Mac Admin: OK I'll lift staging-hold for this device and re-run the post_enroll policy. Doing it now.

mdm-bot: Jamf action 'lift-staging-hold' executed by Rina at 2026-09-05T08:01:12Z.

Rina - Mac Admin: Try `sudo jamf policy -trigger post_enroll` again and then `profiles status -type configuration`.

Jules Park: Re-ran it: now shows "Installing profile 'com.redwood.security.kext'... Success". `profiles status -type configuration` shows the kext and a profile for "SystemPolicyKernelExtension: allow com.example.kext". FileVault still off.

Rina - Mac Admin: Good. FileVault will be enabled by policy once the escrow agent runs; force it with `sudo jamf policy -id 9245` (FileVault enable policy) if you want to encrypt now. Also run the macOS update: `sudo softwareupdate -ia --verbose`.

Jules Park: Ran the FileVault policy, it started encrypting and reported a recovery key escrowed to Jamf. Update now progressing, reboot required. Any chance of temporary admin to install Rosetta after reboot?

Sam (IT): No need, your Jamf-managed policies will install Rosetta if needed. If something pops up requiring an admin password we'll step in. Enjoy first-day setup! :tada:

Jules Park: Rebooted, updates finished, FileVault encrypting in background, all managed profiles present. Thanks everyone for the quick help.

Rina - Mac Admin: Welcome aboard Jules! If you want we can schedule a 15-min check-in to confirm provisioning finished after encryption completes.

Jules Park: Appreciate it, I'll ping when it's finished.
